code_actions.rationale: Provider documents septic shock with lactate 5.1 mmol/L and vasopressor initiation; policy requires A41.9/R65.21 combination and assigns MCC.

Admission notes document multifocal community-acquired pneumonia but do not identify Streptococcus pneumoniae; later hospital course documents Pseudomonas VAP. Recode to unspecified pneumonia (J18.9) for POA admission pneumonia.
Chart documents a hospital-acquired ventilator-associated pneumonia treated for Pseudomonas after bronchoscopy; policy classifies J95.851 as MCC and requires POA=N.
Discharge summary documents renal recovery and that hemodialysis was discontinued prior to transfer - dependence on dialysis (Z99.2) is not supported at discharge and should be removed.

Billed as an open-approach tracheostomy, but the operative note documents a bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy. The open-approach PCS code is not supported by the procedure note; remove and replace with the appropriate percutaneous tracheostomy PCS code.

discharge_disposition: 63 - Discharged/transferred to a Medicare-certified long-term care hospital (LTCH)

evidence.quote: In the ED the patient met criteria for septic shock with a lactate of 5.1 mmol/L that failed to clear after a 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid bolus. Given profound hypoxemic respiratory failure and depressed mental status the patient underwent rapid-sequence intubation, and broad-spectrum antimicrobials and vasopressor support were initiated.

Hospital Course Rosalind Ochoa presented with septic shock and severe multifocal pneumonia, was intubated for hypoxemic respiratory failure, and required norepinephrine and vasopressin. The course was complicated by ARDS managed with lung-protective ventilation and prone positioning, oliguric acute kidney injury requiring CRRT later transitioned to intermittent hemodialysis, new-onset atrial fibrillation controlled with amiodarone, and a hospital-acquired Pseudomonas pneumonia treated with a targeted course of cefepime after bronchoscopy.

Bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy at the second-third tracheal interspace using serial dilation; tube placed with immediate capnographic confirmation; minimal bleeding; no pneumothorax on post-procedure film.
An extubation attempt failed and reintubation was required, after which a tracheostomy was placed for prolonged ventilation and a PEG for enteral nutrition.

History of Present Illness Rosalind Ochoa is a 70-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, COPD, and prior tobacco use who presented with five days of progressive productive cough, subjective fevers to 39.4°C, pleuritic left-sided chest pain, and worsening dyspnea.

system_note: Claim MR_17 - summary of audit findings and rationale (evidence citations follow). What was billed: principal diagnosis A41.9 with R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock), multiple respiratory/renal MCC/CCs (J96.01, J80, N17.9), ventilator-associated pneumonia (J95.851), organism specification B96.5, and an open-approach tracheostomy (0B110F4) among procedures. Findings and line-level rationale: 1) Sepsis / septic shock (A41.9 principal; R65.21 additional - POA=Y): Provider documentation explicitly diagnoses septic shock with objective hemodynamic and laboratory support on presentation: lactate 5.1 mmol/L, initiation of vasopressors, and emergent intubation (ED/H&P). Evidence: History & Physical (admit) documents "In the ED the patient met criteria for septic shock with a lactate of 5.1 mmol/L that failed to clear after a 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid bolus" and "...vasopressor support were initiated" (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n9, H&P, p.54). Per the sepsis policy, R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) requires provider documentation of septic shock plus vasopressor use and/or lactate elevation; the policy lists these as validation criteria and assigns MCC (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b101, Validation Criteria > Vasopressor criterion; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b93, lactate criterion). Conclusion: A41.9 as principal with R65.21 additional is supported, but the codes' severity flags must reflect the policy (A41.9 / R65.21 = MCC). Evidence: ev1, ev2. 2) Acute respiratory failure (J96.01) and ARDS (J80) (both MCC): The H&P and subsequent ICU notes document hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring intubation and ARDS-level management (ARDSnet, proning consideration). H&P: "...profound hypoxemic respiratory failure ... underwent rapid-sequence intubation" and problem list includes ARDS (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n9, p.54). J96.01 and J80 validation criteria require provider diagnosis plus objective hypoxemia/ventilator support or Berlin criteria; these elements are present in the chart (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b27..b39; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Distress-Syndrome-ARDS-.docx-b33..b52). Evidence: ev1, ev10, ev11. 3) Ventilator-associated pneumonia (J95.851) - severity flag and POA: The chart documents a hospital-acquired ventilator-associated pneumonia with culture-directed therapy for Pseudomonas and lists it as hospital-day event; the Discharge/Transfer Summary documents "resolved ventilator-associated pneumonia (Pseudomonas)" and treatment with cefepime after bronchoscopy (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n1213, Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.913). Per the VAP policy, J95.851 carries MCC and must have POA=N (J95.851 is an HAC by definition) (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8 and -b73). In the claim J95.851 is present POA=N but was billed as CC-level; policy requires MCC. Action: keep J95.851 but correct severity to MCC. Evidence: ev5, ev6. 4) Pneumonia due to Streptococcus pneumoniae (J13) - unsupported as coded for present-on-admission: The admission H&P documents "severe multifocal community-acquired pneumonia" but does not document Streptococcus pneumoniae as the causative organism on admission (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n9, H&P, p.54). Subsequent hospital-course documentation identifies a hospital-acquired Pseudomonas VAP treated after bronchoscopy (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n1213, Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.913). No provider note in the retrieved record explicitly documents Streptococcus pneumoniae as the organism present on admission. Action: recode J13 -> J18.9 (pneumonia, unspecified) as the present-on-admission pneumonia (supports sequencing and avoids assigning an unsupported organism-specific code on admission). Evidence: ev12, ev5. 5) Acute kidney injury (N17.9) and dialysis-status code (Z99.2): Nephrology documents oliguric AKI meeting criteria for renal replacement therapy and recommends CVVHDF (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n28, Nephrology Consultation, p.556). That supports N17.9 (CC). However the discharge/transfer summary documents renal recovery and states "hemodialysis was discontinued" (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n1213, Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.913). Z99.2 (dependence on renal dialysis) is billed POA=N but the record documents that dialysis was discontinued and renal function recovered prior to transfer. Action: keep N17.9 (AKI) but remove Z99.2 (status code left active after resolution). Evidence: ev3, ev13. 6) Tracheostomy procedure code technique mismatch (0B110F4 billed = bypass trachea to cutaneous with tracheostomy device, open approach): The chart contains a Procedure Note documenting a bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy with serial dilation and tube placement (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n98, Procedure Note - Percutaneous Dilational Tracheostomy, p.228). The claim billed an open-approach tracheostomy (0B110F4). These two cannot both be correct. Per the conflict annotation the procedure note is the authoritative documentation for the technique. Action: remove the billed open-approach tracheostomy code (0B110F4) because the operative note documents a percutaneous approach; the record supports a percutaneous dilational tracheostomy instead (the correct ICD-10-PCS percutaneous tracheostomy code should replace 0B110F4 in coding correction). Evidence: ev7. 7) Other procedures and status codes: Endotracheal intubation (0BH17EZ), central/arterial access (02HV33Z, 03HY32Z), insertion of feeding device (0DH60UZ/PEG), bronchoscopy (0BJ08ZZ), prolonged mechanical ventilation >96 hours (5A1D90Z), and renal replacement procedure codes (5A1D80Z / dialysis) are supported by the clinical course (ED/H&P, nephrology consult, discharge summary documenting prolonged ventilation, tracheostomy placement, CRRT -> IHD, and targeted bronchoscopy-directed therapy). Evidence: ev1, ev3, ev9, ev5. Summary of required corrections (claim-level): - Principal diagnosis sequencing (A41.9 principal; R65.21 additional) remains clinically appropriate and supported; however A41.9 and R65.21 must carry MCC severity flags per policy. - J13 (pneumonia due to Streptococcus pneumoniae) is not supported for present-on-admission organism-specific assignment; recode to J18.9 (pneumonia, unspecified) POA=Y. - J95.851 (VAP) is supported but should be MCC (policy) and POA=N (already POA=N on the claim). Correct severity to MCC. - Remove Z99.2 (dependence on renal dialysis) because the record documents that hemodialysis was discontinued and renal function recovered prior to transfer. - Remove 0B110F4 (open-approach tracheostomy) because the Procedure Note documents a bronchoscopic percutaneous dilational tracheostomy (replace with the correct percutaneous tracheostomy PCS code via coder action). Key evidence (document/section/page): H&P (NOTE-...-n9, p.54) for admission physiology, ED note (NOTE-...-n8, p.54) for intubation/vasopressor start, Nephrology consult (NOTE-...-n28, p.556) for RRT indication, Procedure Note (NOTE-...-n98, p.228) for percutaneous tracheostomy, Discharge/Transfer Summary (NOTE-...-n1213, p.913) for VAP organism and statement that dialysis was discontinued, and the governing condition policies for sepsis, ARDS, ARF, VAP and AKI (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-*, RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-*, RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Distress-Syndrome-ARDS-.docx-*, RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-*, RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Kidney-Injury.docx-*). See evidence_cited for verbatim quotes and exact pages. Conclusion / determination: Finding. The claim has multiple supported major diagnoses (sepsis with septic shock, ARDS, acute respiratory failure, AKI, VAP) - those remain but with corrected severity flags and one principal coding retained. Corrective actions needed: recode J13 -> J18.9 (POA=Y), change severity flags (A41.9, R65.21, J96.01, J80, J95.851 to MCC where applicable), remove Z99.2, and remove 0B110F4 and replace with the percutaneous tracheostomy PCS code. Detailed line-level code decisions and the corrected code lists follow in the report.
rationale_letter: To: Coding/Medical Record Department Re: MR_17 - DRG audit determination (admit 07/01/2026 - transfer 11/21/2026) We performed a DRG-level three-way audit comparing the claim lines to the medical record and the applicable coding validation policies. Based on our review of the physician documentation and the governing DRG policies, we have found coding discrepancies requiring correction. Finding(s) (summary): 1. Procedure technique mismatch - the claim bills an open tracheostomy (ICD-10-PCS 0B110F4), but the operative/procedure note documents a bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy (Procedure Note, p.228). The billed open-approach code is not supported by the record; the provider-performed percutaneous technique is documented and should be coded instead. (Evidence relied on: Procedure Note - Bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n98, p.228; see ev7.) 2. Unsupported organism-specific pneumonia on admission - J13 (pneumonia due to Streptococcus pneumoniae) is billed as present on admission, but the admission H&P documents "severe multifocal community-acquired pneumonia" without organism identification, and the hospital course later documents a hospital-acquired Pseudomonas ventilator-associated pneumonia treated after bronchoscopy. The record does not support Streptococcus pneumoniae as the organism present on admission. Recommend recoding J13 -> J18.9 (pneumonia, unspecified) POA=Y for the admission pneumonia. (Evidence: H&P admission and Discharge/Transfer Summary, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n9 p.54 and NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n1213 p.913; see ev12, ev5.) 3. CC/MCC severity flag corrections - policy guidance requires certain codes to carry MCC status. Specifically, A41.9 (sepsis, unspecified organism) and R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) meet MCC-level criteria given documented lactate 5.1 mmol/L and vasopressor administration (provider-documented septic shock). J95.851 (ventilator-associated pneumonia) is an MCC-level code by policy and must be POA=N. These severity flags on the claim must be corrected to reflect the policy. (Evidence: H&P/ED documentation of septic shock with lactate and vasopressors, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n9 p.54; and policy RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx and RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx; see ev1, ev2, ev6.) 4. Status code left active after resolution - Z99.2 (dependence on renal dialysis) is coded but the discharge/transfer summary documents renal recovery and that hemodialysis was discontinued prior to transfer; Z99.2 is not supported at discharge and should be removed. N17.9 (acute kidney injury) is supported by nephrology documentation and should remain. (Evidence: Nephrology consult documenting RRT initiation criteria, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n28 p.556; Discharge summary documenting renal recovery and dialysis discontinuation, NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_17.pdf-n1213 p.913; see ev3, ev13.) Corrective action requested (summary): - Retain A41.9 as principal diagnosis (POA=Y) and R65.21 as additional (MCC); set both to MCC per policy. - Recode J13 -> J18.9 (pneumonia, unspecified) POA=Y (admission pneumonia) unless provider documents Streptococcus pneumoniae as the cause on admission. - Retain J96.01 and J80 (both MCC) as documented. - Retain J95.851 (VAP) but change severity to MCC and maintain POA=N. - Remove Z99.2 (dependence on renal dialysis) because the chart documents dialysis discontinued and renal recovery prior to transfer. - Remove billed open tracheostomy code 0B110F4 and replace with the appropriate percutaneous tracheostomy ICD-10-PCS code to reflect the documented bronchoscopic percutaneous dilational tracheostomy (see Procedure Note, p.228). Basis: The corrections are grounded in explicit provider documentation in the chart (admission H&P, ED note, nephrology consult, procedure note, and discharge/transfer summary) and the facility DRG coding policies (Sepsis/Septic Shock, ARF, ARDS, VAP, AKI) that define required objective and documentation elements for MCC/CC assignment and approach-specific procedure coding. Representative citations are provided below. If you disagree with the recoding recommendations (for example if a provider note exists elsewhere in the chart confirming Streptococcus pneumoniae at admission or if a different tracheostomy technique note is present), please provide the exact note (document name and page) so we can reassess. Otherwise, please update the claim as outlined above. Sincerely, Clinical DRG Auditor
